title: Kafka Consumer Groups
description: Understand consumer groups, partition assignment strategies, and rebalancing in Kafka.

data.text: Consumer groups are Kafka's mechanism for horizontal scaling and fault-tolerant consumption. Each consumer group represents a logical subscriber to one or more topics. Within a group, each partition is consumed by exactly one consumer, enabling parallel processing while maintaining message order.

When consumers join a group, Kafka's group coordinator assigns partitions to consumers using a partition assignment strategy. The default strategy, RangeAssignor, assigns contiguous ranges of partitions to consumers. For more even distribution, CooperativeStickyAssignor minimizes partition movement during rebalances.

data.text: When consumers join or leave a group, Kafka triggers a rebalance to reassign partitions. During a rebalance, the group pauses consumption while partitions are redistributed. Long rebalances can increase consumer lag. To minimize disruption, use CooperativeStickyAssignor and keep consumer instances stable.

data.title: Rebalancing Best Practices
items: Use CooperativeStickyAssignor for minimal partition movement during rebalances.
Avoid frequent consumer restarts by handling errors gracefully inside the consume loop.
Set `session.timeout.ms` and `heartbeat.interval.ms` appropriately to detect failed consumers quickly.
Keep consumer group IDs stable in production; changing the group ID causes a full rebalance and offset reset.

data.title: Consumer Lag
data.text: Consumer lag measures how far behind a consumer group is from the latest message offset. Monitor lag in production using Kafka's consumer group command or a monitoring tool like Prometheus with JMX exporter.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Consumer groups allow multiple consumers to share the work of reading a topic.
Each partition in a group is consumed by exactly one consumer instance.
Rebalancing redistributes partitions when consumers join or leave.
data.takeaway: Consumer groups are the scalability primitive in Kafka; understanding assignment and rebalancing prevents production surprises.
